newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-RANGERS BEAT MARINERS IN RECORD STRIKEOUT SHOW.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-RANGERS BEAT MARINERS IN RECORD STRIKEOUT SHOW.

text.p: Damon Buford's solo homer in the top of the ninth snapped a tie and led the Texas Rangers to a 4-2 victory over the Seattle Mariners Sunday in a game that saw a major-league record 31 strikeouts.

Seattle starter Randy Johnson had 14 strikeouts but no part of the decision. Rangers starter Bobby Witt, who allowed two runs and eight hits over 6 2/3 innings, had a season-high nine strikeouts but also no decision.
Danny Patterson (6-3) got the win with 1 2/3 innings of hitless relief. John Wetteland tossed a perfect ninth for his 19th save.
After six consecutive Rangers had struck out, Buford sent a 2-2 pitch from reliever Bobby Ayala (6-3) into the left-field seats, giving Texas a 3-2 lead.
Ivan Rodriguez later added a sacrifice fly to give the Rangers a split of the four-game series. Texas won in Seattle for just the sixth time in its last 30 games.
Texas struck out 18 times, tying its team record last done on September 27, 1992 -- against Johnson.

"When you come in here with a full house and Randy pitching, there's not much room for error," Texas manager Johnny Oates said. "It's much nicer when you win 4-2 with the 31 punchouts. When is Randy not tough? Day in and day out, he's the one guy you really don't want to face.
"We were fortunate that his pitch count got up today and he had to leave after seven."
Johnson, who allowed an unearned run and eight hits with 21 strikeouts in two previous starts against Texas this season, yielded two runs and five hits.
"It's frustrating for everyone when we lose," Seattle catcher Dan Wilson said. "Randy pitched a great game and kept us in it late. We just weren't able to hold on."
Paul Sorrento homered for Seattle and the Mariners knotted it in the sixth on Jay Buhner's 23rd homer of the season. It was also Buhner's 1,000th career hit.
Mariners star Ken Griffey Jr missed the game to attend the funeral of his mother-in-law.
The previous major-league record for combined strikeouts in a game was 30, set on April 19, 1986, when 18 Mariners and 12 Athletics went down.
In Kansas City, Frank Thomas and Albert Belle each homered and drove in three runs to lead the Chicago White Sox to their seventh straight win, 7-6 over the Royals.
The Royals have lost a club-record 12 in a row. The Chisox have won all seven meetings this season.
Carlos Castillo (1-1) notched the win by pitching 3 2/3 scoreless innings of relief. Jim Pittsley (2-7) took the loss.
In Minnesota, Jim Thome and Brian Giles each homered, drove in three runs and scored twice as the Cleveland Indians pounded the Twins 12-5 for their third straight win.

Giles and Omar Vizquel collected three hits each and Vizquel and Marquis Grissom also scored twice for the Indians, who had 15 hits off slumping starter LaTroy Hawkins (1-5) and four relievers. Every Indians starter had at least one hit except Grissom, who had an 11-game hitting streak snapped.

Julio Franco stole home on the front end of a double-steal in the sixth for the Indians, who remained 2 1/2 games in front of the White Sox atop the American League Central Division. The Twins have lost three in a row.
In Baltimore, former Oriole Jack Voigt continued to hurt his old club with a two-run homer as the Milwaukee Brewers swept the O's for the first time in almost six years, 6-4.
Voigt, who homered in the first game of the series Friday, drove a 2-1 pitch from starter Mike Mussina (10-3) over the wall in left with two outs in the sixth for a 5-2 lead.
Prior to the series with Baltimore, the 31-year-old utility player had two homers and eight RBI in 14 games for the Brewers this season.
The slumping Orioles have dropped a season-high six consecutive games.
In Boston, six pitchers combined on a seven-hitter and Shawn Green hit a two-run homer for the second straight game as the Toronto Blue Jays edged the Red Sox 3-2 for their third win in a row.
Green has three consecutive games with the winning RBI.
Tim Wakefield (3-10) returned to the starting rotation and tossed a six-hitter in a losing effort.

In New York, Bob Higginson went 4-for-5 with a solo homer and three RBI while Willie Blair (7-4) surrendered just one run over seven innings as the Detroit Tigers salvaged the finale of a four-game series and snapped a 10-game losing streak against the Yankees, 3-1.
Dwight Gooden (3-2) took the loss.

In Oakland, four pitchers -- knuckleballer Dennis Springer, Shigetoshi Hasegawa (2-4), Rich DeLucia and Troy Percival -- combined on a four-hitter and Tony Phillips had two hits and two RBI as the Anaheim Angels used nine walks to get their 11th straight win over the Athletics, 5-3.
Garret Anderson contributed three hits and scored a run for Anaheim, which has won six in a row overall and five straight on the road. The Angels improved to 10-0 against Oakland this season.
